acme_sre: Hey team — after the scheduled cert rotation at 00:12 UTC our prod API started returning 502s for services inside the customer's VPC. External calls are fine. Internal clients see TLS verify errors. Can you triage? :eyes:

john_support: Can you paste the minimal repro (openssl/curl) and any HAProxy/nginx logs you have? Also which account/tenant is this?

acme_sre: tenant=acme-inc. Quick repro from one of their app hosts (10.0.32.5):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.acme.internal:443 -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.acme.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=acme-intermediate
---
# no intermediate presented by endpoint
```
Server logs show: `tls: handshake failure: remote error: bad certificate` and HAProxy 502s.

meera: Two quick checks: 1) Is the rotator uploading the full chain (leaf + intermediates)? 2) Are OCSP/CRL responders reachable from the VPC (egress allowlist)? Missing both will cause verification failures.

acme_sre: ran a curl to OCSP responder from the same host, timed out: `curl -v https://ocsp.acme-ca.com/` -> hangs then `Connection timed out`. Dig output: `dig ocsp.acme-ca.com +short` -> `10.20.30.40` (split-horizon DNS returns private IP). Their NAT/firewall restricts outbound IPs; we've seen the CA expect public egress.

sasha: That smells like two independent faults colliding: a mis-bundled cert (server not sending intermediate) + OCSP host resolving to an internal/private IP that cannot complete egress path. Steps: check the rotator job that wrote the cert to the LB and confirm bundle flag. Also validate their VPC NAT/firewall allowlist includes the CA's public OCSP IPs.

acme_sre: rotator job config attached from the customer's rotator microservice (redacted):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: acme-api-cert
data:
  tls.crt: |-
    -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n    <leaf cert>\n    -----END CERTIFICATE-----
  tls.key: |-
    -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n    <priv>\n    -----END PRIVATE KEY-----
# Note: rotator had `bundle: false` in config map
```
So it looks like the intermediate wasn't included.

meera: That explains the "no intermediate presented" in openssl. But normally clients can fetch intermediate via AIA/Issuer URL or OCSP if allowed. In this case AIA resolves to a host that resolves internally and is not reachable externally, so the client can't fetch the missing cert.

john_support: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) Ask rotator to re-deploy with full-chain PEM (leaf + intermediate). 2) Ask customer to temporarily allow egress to the CA's OCSP/CRL IPs or add a proxy rule. 3) As a short-term workaround, tenant can pin the intermediate in their trust store (last resort).

acme_sre: I'll coordinate with their infra. Re-upload command I used to test on an internal test VM (worked):
```
# generate combined PEM
cat leaf.pem intermediate.pem > fullchain.pem
# test locally
openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:8443 -cert fullchain.pem -showcerts
```
If we upload fullchain to HAProxy (via rotator) the openssl verify passes locally.

sasha: Also confirm there isn't a transparent proxy rewriting responses. They mentioned a private DNS view that maps ocsp.acme-ca.com to 10.20.30.40 which is their internal OCSP forwarder — does that forward outbound properly? If not, adding the CA's public IPs to the allowlist or fixing the forwarder NAT should be done.

acme_sre: Customer checked their NAT GW logs: outbound to 93.184.220.10 (one of CA's public OCSP IPs) is being dropped by a tenant firewall rule that only allows a small subset of destinations. They will add the CA IPs. Rotator team also agreed to push a fix to set `bundle: true` by default for this tenant.

oncall-bot: rotator-deploy: deployment/rotator-acme v2.7.3 triggered by @sasha — https://deployments.redwood/rotator-acme/2.7.3 :white_check_mark:

acme_sre: after change: re-uploaded fullchain and customer added egress rule. Quick verification from inside the VPC:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.acme.internal:443 -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Acme CA, CN = Acme Root
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=acme-intermediate
 1 s:/CN=acme-intermediate
   i:/CN=acme-root
---
verify OK
```
Errors dropped, no 502s in the last 20m. :tada:

meera: Great. Follow-ups: 1) Rotator default to bundle=true for private VPC tenants (bug). 2) Add a KB article for customers about split-horizon DNS + OCSP egress pitfalls. 3) We'll add an automated check during rotation: resolve OCSP/AIA from the customer's control plane network and warn if resolution points to private IPs.

john_support: Filed support ticket #S-2026-451 and linked this thread. Marking resolved but keep monitoring for 24h. :thumbsup:
